candidates.exact_span: The percent solids of sewage sludge that contains unstabilized solids generated in a primary wastewater treatment process shall be equal to or greater than 90% based on the moisture content and total solids prior to mixing with other materials.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a numeric percent-solids floor (≥90%); different readings of moisture/total-solids basis or whether sludge qualifies as containing unstabilized primary solids would change which limit applies and whether a reported solids measurement exceeds it.

candidates.exact_span: Unstabilized solids are defined as organic materials in sewage sludge that have not been treated in either an aerobic or anaerobic treatment process.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines when Alternative 8's 90% limit is operative; whether sludge is treated aerobically/anaerobically or deemed unstabilized changes whether the numeric limit is in scope for a given measurement.

candidates.exact_span: No significant amount of the sewage sludge shall be present on the land surface within one hour after the sewage sludge is injected.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a time-bound surface-presence requirement keyed to an undefined 'significant amount'; different thresholds for significance or timing evidence would change compliance determination against this limit.

candidates.exact_span: When sewage sludge that is injected below the surface of the land is Class A with respect to pathogens, the sewage sludge shall be injected below the land surface within eight hours after being discharged from the pathogen treatment process.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Imposes an eight-hour injection deadline conditional on Class A pathogen status; resolving Class A classification, discharge timing, and pathogen-treatment discharge time affects both enforceable limit comparison (A) and whether this conditional obligation was applicable (B).

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge applied to the land surface or placed on a surface disposal site shall be incorporated into the soil within six hours after application to or placement on the land.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a six-hour incorporation deadline; different interpretations of application/placement time or incorporation completion would change whether reported timing data exceed the limit.

candidates.exact_span: When sewage sludge that is incorporated into the soil is Class A with respect to pathogens, the sewage sludge shall be applied to or placed on the land within eight hours after being discharged from the pathogen treatment process.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Imposes an eight-hour land-application deadline conditional on Class A status; Class A determination and event timing affect both limit exceedance analysis (A) and conditional monitoring/applicability (B).

candidates.exact_span: Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP) Test - Once/Permit Life, performed within one year from the effective date of the permit
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies a one-time-per-permit-life TCLP obligation with a one-year post-effective-date window; different readings of permit life, effective date, or whether the test was satisfied change required monitoring (B) and how absent TCLP results are classified (C).
Establishes annual PCB monitoring; whether this requirement was in force for a given FY2025 period affects monitoring-obligation evaluation (B) and the semantics of missing PCB results (C).

candidates.exact_span: All other pollutants shall be monitored at the frequency shown below:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Scopes pollutant monitoring to the tiered schedule below rather than named pollutants above; interpretation of which parameters fall under 'all other pollutants' changes which frequency obligations apply.

candidates.computation_change_reason: Links monitoring frequency to sludge quantity tier; whether annual quantity falls below 290 metric tons changes required monitoring cadence (B) and how missing results for that tier are interpreted (C).

candidates.locator: page 6, section part_i, Monitoring Requirements table
candidates.computation_change_reason: Quarterly monitoring applies within this sludge-volume band; boundary interpretation at 290 or 1,500 metric tons changes obligation frequency (B) and missing-data expectations (C).

candidates.locator: page 6, section part_i, Monitoring Requirements table
candidates.computation_change_reason: Bi-monthly monitoring applies within this band; different sludge-total calculations crossing 1,500 or 15,000 metric tons change required monitoring (B) and adequacy of evidence for absent results (C).

candidates.locator: page 6, section part_i, Monitoring Requirements table
candidates.computation_change_reason: Monthly monitoring applies at or above 15,000 metric tons; whether quantity meets this threshold changes monitoring obligations (B) and whether missing monthly results indicate inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.locator: page 6, section part_i, Monitoring Requirements table footnote
candidates.exact_span: *Either the amount of bulk sewage sludge applied to the land or the amount of sewage sludge received by a person who prepares sewage sludge that is sold or given away in a bag or other container for application to the land (dry weight basis).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines which sludge quantities count toward tier selection and requires dry-weight basis; choosing bulk-applied vs received-for-bagged-product quantity or dry-weight conversion method can shift tier boundaries and thus monitoring frequency (B) and missing-evidence classification (C).

candidates.exact_span: Representative samples of sewage sludge shall be collected and analyzed in accordance with the methods referenced in 40 CFR 503.8(b).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Prescribes sampling and analytical methods for reported values; whether samples were representative and analyzed under 503.8(b) methods affects comparability of measurements to numeric limits (A) and whether monitoring was performed as required (B).

candidates.exact_span: For those permittees meeting Class A or B pathogen reduction requirements and that meet the cumulative loading rates in Table 2 below, or the Class B pathogen reduction requirements and contain
candidates.computation_change_reason: Conditions applicability of Section II requirements on Class A/B pathogen status and Table 2 cumulative loading rates (or alternate Class B pollutant-concentration path referenced in the heading); unresolved classification or loading-rate satisfaction changes which limits and monitoring rules are in scope (A,B) and whether absent evidence reflects non-applicability vs unresolved obligation (C).
